questions.q: After the newly formed project team has gone through many conflicts between the team members, the project team starts to function as a collective body. Team members know their places on the team and how they relate to and interface with all the other members. They are starting to work together.What is the best leadership style to lead a team at this stage?" *

o.t: Provide a more directive than supportive leadership.
Provide a more supportive than directive leadership.
Provide high levels of both directive and supportive leadership.
Provide low levels of both directive and supportive leadership.

questions.e: The team has moved past conflict and is working together, meaning they are in the Norming stage of Tuckman’s Ladder. At this stage, the leader should be more supportive rather than directive.

questions.q: Victor is a project manager for a software project. Two team members Kevin and Tom are having a conflict. Kevin explains his opinion, and presents a possible solution. But before Tom starts to explain his opinion, the project manager says, “It is OK, I’ve heard enough, and I’ve decided to go with the solution of Kevin.” This is an example of: *
questions.e: The project manager imposed a decision without listening to all viewpoints, which is an example of the Forcing conflict resolution technique.

questions.q: Michael is managing an accounting software project. He finds that bringing all of his team members together into a single room to work increases their communication, and decreases misunderstandings. This is referred to as a: *
questions.e: Colocation involves placing team members in the same physical location to improve communication and teamwork.

questions.q: XYZ organiztion has initiated a new software project. The new project will adopt an adaptive development approach. Resources are being carefully selected for this project because this project is for a new customer and it is expected to have a long term partnership with this customer. Which of the following resources types will be suitable for this project? *

o.t: People who have deep specializations in one domain.

questions.e: T-shaped resources are individuals who have deep expertise in one area (the vertical bar of the T) and broad knowledge in other areas (the horizontal bar of the T). In an adaptive development approach, such as Agile, T-shaped individuals are valuable because they can contribute in multiple areas, collaborate effectively with team members, and adapt to changing project requirements.

questions.q: Helena is a team member who has recently joined a running construction project. She noticed that there is a difference between leadership styles of Kevin, the project manager of the current project and Andrea the project manager of her previous project. Kevin always focuses on goals and achievements, while Andrea focuses on team members learning, development and relationships. What leadership styles do they adopt? *

o.t: Kevin adopts transactional style, while Andrea adopts charismatic style.
Kevin adopts transformational style, while Andrea adopts servant leader style.
Kevin adopts transactional style, while Andrea adopts servant leader style.
Kevin adopts laissez-faire style, while Andrea adopts interactional style.

questions.e: Kevin's focus on goals and achievements aligns with a transactional leadership style, which emphasizes performance and reward-based motivation. Andrea's focus on team members' learning, development, and relationships aligns with a servant leader style, which prioritizes the growth and well-being of team members and fosters a supportive team environment.

questions.q: The project manager for the new project notices that the meeting room seats and air conditioner are not good. She turns her attention to influencing the organization to improve the team’s working conditions. Which motivational theory is she following? *
questions.e: Herzberg's Motivation-Hygiene Theory (also known as the Two-Factor Theory) suggests that there are certain factors in the workplace that cause job satisfaction (motivators) and a separate set of factors that cause dissatisfaction (hygiene factors). Improving working conditions, such as seating and air conditioning, addresses hygiene factors, which, when inadequate, can cause dissatisfaction.

questions.q: The project manager has called for a meeting for the project team to discuss the high-level plan of the project and to start developing the subsidiary plans. Most of the project team members are having disagreements on how the work will be done as this is the first time for them to work together. Referring to Tuckman ladder, this phase is known as: *
questions.e: The Storming phase is where conflicts arise as team members try to establish their roles and ways of working.

questions.q: You are an agile practicioner to be assigned to a new project. There are two teams in the organization who can work on this project. Team A has John a business analyst, Mark a UI designer, Steve a coder and Smith a system tester. They are all experts in their fields. Team B has Mathew and Ann who can both work as business analyst and UI designer as well and Chris and Sandra who can both work as coder and system tester as well. Which team will you prefer to work with and why? *

o.t: Team A because team members are generalizing specialists.
Team B because team members are generalizing specialists.
Team A because team members are traditional specialists.
Team B because team members are traditional specialists.

questions.e: In Agile, having team members who are generalizing specialists (or T-shaped individuals) is highly beneficial. This means that members have deep expertise in at least one area but also have skills and experience in other areas. This allows for greater flexibility, collaboration, and the ability to adapt to changing project needs. Team B's members, who can perform multiple roles, embody this concept.

questions.q: During the testing phase of a technical project, the project manager discovers some issues with the final product and subsequently learns that after negotiations, important product features were excluded from the contract's scope in an effort to minimize costs for the client. What should the project manager do to resolve the issue? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the sponsor to make a decision to redefine the scope and solve the problem.
Work with the client to negotiate and ensure the inclusion of the missing crucial features in the project.
Continue with the project as planned and register the contract scope issue in the issue log.
Review the lessons learned to find a solution for contract negotiation and scope issues.

questions.e: The project manager should address the issue directly with the client to negotiate the inclusion of the missing crucial features. This approach ensures that the final product meets the client's needs and expectations. Escalating to the sponsor or simply logging the issue does not directly resolve the problem, while reviewing lessons learned is more about preventing future issues rather than addressing the current one.

questions.q: Alfrid is attending a project management training session. He is watching the speaker to pick up physical gestures and facial expressions. He confirms he is listening, expresses agreement or disagreement and summarizing what he says. Which communication skill does he have? *
questions.e: Active listening involves fully concentrating, understanding, responding, and remembering what is being said. It includes observing body language and facial expressions, providing feedback, and confirming understanding. Alfrid demonstrates active listening by watching the speaker's gestures, confirming he is listening, expressing agreement or disagreement, and summarizing the speaker's points.

questions.q: Mary, the project manager, sent a text message to Tom, a project stakeholder, using the company’s instant messaging system. When he received it, Tom called her back. Which of the following is true about this situation? *

o.t: Mary encoded the text message; Tom decoded it, and then encoded his feedback message.
Mary decoded her text message; Tom encoded his phone call and decoded the feedback.
Tom sent feedback to Mary, who encoded it.
Mary decoded her text message and Tom encoded his feedback.

questions.e: In the communication process, encoding is the act of creating a message to be sent, and decoding is the act of interpreting the received message. Mary encoded her message when she sent the text, and Tom decoded it upon receipt. Tom then encoded his feedback when he called her, and Mary would decode the feedback when she received the call.

questions.q: A project team member sent a confidential information to a third party by mistake. The project manager is very angry and he insists on punishing the team member. What could have prevented this situation? *
questions.e: The communications management plan outlines how communications should be conducted, including protocols for handling confidential information. Properly following and reviewing this plan could have prevented the accidental disclosure by ensuring that all team members are aware of the procedures and restrictions related to confidential information.

questions.q: Catherine is managing a project to author a book about using earned value management in construction project. She asked Maria, a technical writer, to help her in this project. Maria advised her to pay attentions to the following points: using correct grammar and spelling using concise expressions and eliminating excess words, having clear purpose, using markers such as introduction and summaries of the ideas, and controlling the flow of words and ideas using graphics. Which techniques did Maria advised Catherine to use? *
questions.e: The 5C's of written communication are Correct grammar and spelling, Concise expressions, Clear purpose, Coherent structure (including the use of markers like introductions and summaries), and Controlling the flow of ideas using graphics. Maria's advice aligns with these principles.

questions.q: Samuel has just been assigned as a project manager for an ongoing tele-communications project instead of Gary who has recently resigned from the company. The project is very large and has a budget of 5,000,000$. The project is being performed in two cities using 75 team members. There was a problem regarding the testing activities that Samuel doesn't know who is responsible to perform these activities. What should he do? *

o.t: He should refer to the project sponsor for guidance.
He should call Gary to ask him about each one's role.
He should consult the resources management plan.
He should consult the responsibility assignment matrix.

questions.e: The Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) is a tool used to assign project tasks to team members. It clearly defines who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed (RACI) for each task. Consulting the RAM will provide Samuel with the information about who is responsible for the testing activities.

questions.q: Midway through the project, a conflict arises between the project manager and a team member. The project manager believes that a specific task should be executed by the team member, while the team member is convinced that it should be executed by another person. The team member escalates the situation to his functional manager. In order to resolve the conflict, the project manager should consult _________. *
questions.e: The RACI chart (Responsibility Assignment Matrix) is a tool that clearly outlines the roles and responsibilities of each team member in relation to project tasks. Consulting the RACI chart will help resolve the conflict by clarifying who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for the specific task in question.

questions.q: Monica is a project manager on a large software project. The customer required a change to a major work package. She evaluates the impact of the change and informs the customer with the impact on project schedule and budget. But the customer won't allow any change to the schedule and won't pay anything more for implementing the change. Monica explains that the proposed change in outside the document scope of the original work. The customer tells Monica that he doesn't care what was in the original scope and that she needs to implement the change with no impact to schedule or budget. What conflict resolution technique is the customer using? *
questions.e: Forcing is a conflict resolution technique where one party insists on their viewpoint at the expense of others. It is a win-lose approach where the person using the technique is focused on achieving their desired outcome without regard for the concerns or inputs of others. In this case, the customer is using forcing by insisting that the change be implemented without any impact to the schedule or budget, regardless of the original scope or the project manager's concerns.

questions.q: Peter is a project manager for a tele-communication project in a multinational company. The project team members are located in three countries with different time zones. As per the communications management plan, the project team has a weekly status meeting through videoconferencing. Which communication method are they using? *
questions.e: nteractive communication involves the exchange of information between two or more parties in real time. Videoconferencing for weekly status meetings is a form of interactive communication, as it allows for immediate feedback and interaction among the project team members.

questions.q: Which of the following represents a lose-lose negotiation? *

o.t: The project manager decides to give up on his own approach and use the approach provided by Mark in order to gain confidence.
The technical team negotiates different approaches and they will implement Phillip's approach rather than the approach provided by Mary.
The project manager has agreed with the two team members who are in a conflict to compromise.
The supplier succeeded in negotiation with the procurement manager to reach a fair and reasonable price for the service which he will provide.

questions.e: A compromise is often considered a lose-lose negotiation because both parties give up something to reach a middle ground. Neither side gets exactly what they want, so both may feel they have lost something in the negotiation. This contrasts with win-win solutions where both parties achieve their primary objectives.

questions.q: During an industrial project, two team members are in conflict because of difference in opinions concerning the correct order of steps to test the final product of the project. Who is initially responsible for resolving this conflict? *
questions.e: Team members should first attempt to resolve their own conflicts before involving management.

questions.q: Two team members are having a disagreement over order of activities in your project. A team member thinks that you should document everything before starting work, while the other thinks you can do the work while you finish the documentation. You meet with both of them and listen to their argument. Then you decide that you will document most of it first but will start doing the work when you are 80% done with the documentation. What conflict resolution technique are you using? *
questions.e: Compromise is a conflict resolution technique where each party gives up something to reach a mutually acceptable solution. By deciding to start the work when 80% of the documentation is done, you are finding a middle ground that partially satisfies both team members' preferences.

questions.q: A project team is facing challenges in collaboration as team members struggle to align on their work expectations. As a project manager, you decide to implement a structured approach to improve collaboration. Which of the following techniques would best enhance team collaboration? *

o.t: Escalating team issues to senior management
Assigning work based on functional roles

questions.e: Team-building activities improve trust, communication, and collaboration among team members. This enhances the overall performance and reduces conflicts. The RACI matrix (A) helps define roles, but it does not actively foster collaboration. Escalating issues (C) should be a last resort, and assigning work based on functional roles (D) does not necessarily improve teamwork.

questions.q: A project manager wants to increase team motivation and ensure that the project team remains engaged. According to Herzberg’s two-factor theory, which of the following would be a motivational factor? *
questions.e: Herzberg’s two-factor theory categorizes motivators (which enhance job satisfaction) and hygiene factors (which prevent dissatisfaction). Achievement and recognition are intrinsic motivators that increase engagement and job satisfaction. Job security, working conditions, and salary are hygiene factors that do not increase motivation but prevent dissatisfaction.

questions.q: A project manager leads a highly skilled and self-motivated team. The team members are experts in their respective domains and require minimal supervision. What leadership style would be most effective in this situation? *
questions.e: In a Laissez-faire leadership style, the project manager provides minimal supervision and allows team members to take responsibility for their work. This approach is effective for highly skilled, experienced, and self-motivated teams. In contrast, a directive or autocratic approach (A and C) is more suitable for less experienced teams. Servant leadership (B) focuses on team development but still involves active guidance.

questions.q: Two team members are in a disagreement about the approach to solve a technical problem. As a project manager, you encourage an open discussion, actively listen to their perspectives, and guide them toward finding a mutually beneficial solution. What conflict resolution technique are you using? *
questions.e: The confronting (problem-solving) approach focuses on finding the root cause of a disagreement and working toward the best possible solution. It involves open communication and encourages collaboration. Compromising (A) means both parties give up something, Forcing (B) imposes a solution, and Smoothing (D) minimizes the issue rather than resolving it fully.

questions.q: A project team is in the early stages of team formation. Team members are still learning their roles and responsibilities, and they rely on the project manager for direction. According to Tuckman’s model, what stage is the team currently in? *
questions.e: In the Forming stage of Tuckman’s team development model, team members are still getting acquainted, understanding their roles, and looking to the project manager for guidance. As the team progresses, they move to the Storming stage (conflicts arise), Norming (team cohesion improves), and Performing (team works independently and efficiently).
